newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU leaders gravely concerned over Middle East.
newsitem.headline: EU leaders gravely concerned over Middle East.

text.p: European Union leaders voiced grave concern over the deteriorating Middle East peace process on Saturday and condemned Israeli settlements on occupied Palestinian land.

At a summit in the Irish capital, the 15 leaders addressed a series of hard-hitting demands to Israel to ease a blockade on the Palestinian territories and instructed their special Middle East envoy to promote these as immediate measures.

The detailed list, meant to be confidential but released inadvertently to the media by the EU's Irish presidency, included demands for a commitment to allow more than 50,000 Palestinian workers into Israel in all circumstances.
"The European Council is gravely concerned by the continuing deterioration in the peace process," the statement said. It called on all parties to discourage violence.

The declaration was issued after a week in which two West Bank Jewish settlers were killed by Palestinian gunmen and hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to expand existing settlements.
"The settlements issue is eroding confidence in the peace process," the European statement said. "Settlements contravene international law and are a major obstacle to peace."
The EU said Palestinian social and economic development required the immediate lifting of the Israeli blockade on the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"The European Council urges the Israeli authorities to remove all restrictions except where Israel's legitimate security interests are manifestly engaged, as in the case of acts of terrorism," the draft said.

It warned that the dire economic consequences of the blockade were breeding discontent and violence and had dissipated the optimism generated by the establishment of President Yasser Arafat's self-rule authority.

Among the detailed demands the EU special envoy was instructed to make were: -- a commitment to allow a significant number -- in excess of 50,000 -- of Palestinian workers into Israeli territory in all circumstances -- the elimination of abuses and humiliating practices at checkpoints -- the lifting of all impediments to the transport and export of perishable goods -- the facilitation of the passage of ambulances and medical doctors through checkpoints -- the facilitation of family reunification by broadening the very restrictive definition -- without prejudice to the outcome of negotiations on the status of Jerusalem, taking measures to prevent the separation of family members living in the city.
They added several economic demands including the opening of a Gaza airport and an agreement on the construction of an EU-funded Gaza port.
The EU also urged Israel and the Palestinian Authority to cooperate on security and take all necessary measures to control extremists and combat terrorism.
